text:
support-julie: Heads-up — Acme Inc (private VPC / customer-managed gateway) reported repeated 429 + intermittent auth failures right after their midnight deploy. Customer sees a ~30s burst of connections (2k conn/s) that correlates with their ingest job. Asking for triage and a short-term mitigation they can apply without downtime.

ryan: Can you paste a couple lines of the gateway logs showing x-envoy-ratelimit or upstream 429 headers? Also confirm whether the 429s are from our gateway or from the auth service.

support-julie: Pasted excerpts below (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T09:05:12Z] gw-01 ingress: conn=1987 client=10.2.3.4 path=/v1/generate status=429 x-envoy-ratelimited: true
[2026-03-15T09:05:13Z] auth-svc upstream: request_id=abcd status=503 downstream_status=429
```

marina: Looks like gateway returned 429s after upstream auth started failing with 503. The timing matches a cron job pulse from their side. Kubernetes ingress has an annotation limiting qps to 1000/s per node — still, the bursting connections are saturating the node-level accept queue and exhausting auth concurrency.

alex: Customer also flagged their billing alarm — they saw a spike in token usage during the window and worry about extra charges. They want: 1) immediate mitigation, 2) repro to validate fixes, 3) recommendations to avoid future cost spikes.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed for customer-app v2.4.1 at 2026-03-15T09:05Z

ryan: Proposed short-term mitigations (no downtime):
- Enable connection smoothing on their mgw (token-bucket with 500 qps refill and 10s burst window)
- Configure gateway to prefer returning 503 for excess upstream auth load (fast-fail) instead of queuing behind auth
- Add an ingress annotation to limit new connection rate per pod and enable connection pooling at the gateway

Example k8s annotations to try in staging: 
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "100"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "60000"    # ~1000 rpm per second per pod
    custom.redwood.io/conn-smoothing: "tokenbucket,refill=500,burst=5000,window=10s"
```

marina: For repro in staging: run a controlled client loop to simulate the cron:
```
hey -z 45s -c 500 -q 200 -m POST -D payload.json https://staging-acme.example/v1/generate
```
Capture: tcpdump on mgw, gateway metrics (accept queue, conn_open), envoy stats (`upstream_rq_pending_overflow`), and auth-svc concurrency.

ryan: Also add an envoy filter to short-circuit auth overloads: set `upstream_rq_timeout` lower and enable `upstream_retry_on_503` only for safe endpoints. That reduces cascade failures.

support-julie: Customer permission requested to run staging repro and to temporarily throttle their cron if we need to validate smoothing. They replied: "can throttle for a 30m window but cannot change job cadence long-term."

alex: For billing — suggest we temporarily enable a billing cap on the project to avoid runaway charges and create an alert on token consumption + cost. Also recommend they enable request sampling so we can link spikes to token usage.

marina: Plan for next 24h: 1) Run staging repro with the `hey` command and conn-smoothing annotation; 2) capture pcap + envoy metrics; 3) iterate token-bucket params; 4) apply staging-proven config to prod in a 30m maintenance window and monitor. If prod still shows auth overload, escalate to a short circuit policy (503 fallback) and consider moving heavy cron traffic to a throttled batch queue.

ryan: Long-term suggestions: dedicated capacity (reserved pool) for high-burst customers or a managed ingress proxy that does client-side connection pooling and request coalescing. Also add a standard gradation of rate-limiter profiles (burst-friendly vs smoothing-first) customers can pick.

support-julie: I'll run the staging repro now and share logs + pcap here in ~20m. Assigning follow-ups: @ryan will own gateway config changes, @marina will own repro runs and metrics capture, @alex will own billing safeguards.

opsbot: Created ticket SUPPORT-4821 (cust: acme-inc) and linked this thread.

support-julie: Update: staging repro started at 2026-03-15T09:27Z, capturing tcpdump + envoy metrics. Will post results shortly.
